Auralis Natura · Design Handbook01 · The brand
01

The brand in one page

PhD rigour meeting botanical warmth.

Auralis Natura is the holistic health coaching practice of Dr. rer. nat. Desiree Gruber in Barcelona. The brand's whole job is to make rigorous science feel warm and human — and to be unmistakably honest about what it is.

The positioning

A chemist's precision applied to everyday wellbeing. The competitive gap this brand occupies is the quadrant nobody else holds: high scientific rigour and high human warmth at once. Most wellness brands pick one.

The voice

A brilliant friend who happens to be a scientist. Warm, intelligent, calm, precise. Never breathless, never mystical, never hedging behind jargon. Where evidence is weak, the copy says so — that honesty is a brand asset, not a liability.

The emotional job

Clients arrive depleted and want to feel like themselves again. Every page, card and report should answer that, not a feature list.

What it is never

Not medicine. Not diagnosis. Not "cream + terracotta + serif" wellness pastiche — the palette deliberately moved to warm earth tones, and the geometry to square corners, to sit outside that cliché. See chapter 12 for the guardrails that are legal rather than aesthetic.

The one-line test

Before shipping anything on this brand, read it back and ask: would a thoughtful scientist put their name on this, and would a tired woman at the end of a long week feel welcomed by it? It has to be both. Something that passes only the first reads cold; only the second reads like everyone else.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook02 · Structural decisions
02

Non-negotiables

Eight decisions that define the look.

These were settled by a real print run — the approved business card, design 5B “Reine Fläche”. They are not open questions, and a proposal that breaks one is a proposal to leave the brand.

1

Corners are square

--r and --r-lg are 0px. Never add a border-radius anywhere — this is the single most defining structural decision in the system, and one rounded card undoes it.

2

The seal is the recurring mark

Its signature move is the seal at 10 % opacity, bleeding off the edge as a watermark on large quiet surfaces — hero, dark bands, the CTA card. Never as loud decoration.

3

Clay is the accent, never a field

Role lines, small marks, and one primary clay button per view. Large surfaces are paper, cream or the dark brown band.

4

Gold is structural, not shiny

Hairlines, small caps, the seal — flat --gold / --gold-bright. Mirrored or gradient "chrome" gold was reviewed and rejected as dated.

5

Edges are hairlines; shadows are wide and soft

The printed card's frame is a 0.2 mm hairline. Never tight, dark drop shadows.

6

Restraint is the premium signal

The business card prints at roughly 4 % ink coverage — the paper does the work. The screen equivalent is generous whitespace and few elements per viewport. Resist filling space.

7

“Desiree Gruber” never breaks across lines

At any breakpoint, in any language. Check it at 360 px.

8

Never hyphenate

hyphens: none throughout. German compounds are handled by reducing type size, never by splitting the word. “GE-SUNDHEITSCOACHING” is the failure this rule exists to prevent.

Where these came from. The card handoff describes itself as “the most refined expression of this brand that exists.” Where any older brand note disagrees with these eight, these win — they were measured against ink on paper.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook03 · The mark
03

Logo, lockup and watermark

The botanical seal.

A circular line-drawn botanical crest — the only illustrative element in the whole system, and the thing that makes a surface recognisably Auralis.

Primary · on paper
Gold · on dark bands
Brown · single-colour

The lockup

Seal plus wordmark. Use where the brand has to introduce itself — letterheads, profile headers, the top of a document. On the website the seal alone is usually enough.

The watermark move

The brand's signature treatment: the seal scaled large, set to 10 % opacity, and positioned so it bleeds off the edge of the surface. It reads as texture, not as a logo. Both the cover and the dark band of this handbook use it.

Clear space

Keep free space around the seal equal to at least half its diameter. It never sits inside a box, never gets a keyline, and never appears on a busy photograph.

Minimum size

16 mm in print, 48 px on screen. Below that the botanical linework fills in and it reads as a smudge — use the wordmark alone instead.

Do

  • Use the supplied masters — they have clean alpha channels.
  • Match the variant to the ground: gold on dark, full colour on paper.
  • Let it bleed off the edge when used as a watermark.

Never

  • Recolour, outline, rotate or add effects to the seal.
  • Stretch it — it is circular and stays circular.
  • Use handover/assets/emblem_seal_360.png: a different, busier seal that must never appear on anything customer-facing.

A warm-earth palette.

Cinnamon brown carries the brand; ember clay accents it; amber gold structures it. Every value below is read directly from the design system's token file — these are the live values, not a transcription.

Primary — the dark ground

Modern Materia Medica6
Auralis Natura · Design Handbook04 · Colour

Using the palette

The dark band recipe

Dark sections are not a flat fill. They are a three-stop gradient at 158°:

--forest-soft → --forest at 55 % → --forest-deep, with a --gold-hair hairline on the top edge and the seal watermark bleeding from one corner.

Emphasis, by ground

On light sections, emphasis is ink at weight 600. On dark bands it is amber --gold-bright. Never clay for emphasis text — clay belongs to actions.

The clay discipline

Clay is the most misused token in any system like this. The rule is simple: one primary clay button per view, and clay never fills an area larger than a button or a hairline rule. If a design has two clay buttons competing, one of them is not the primary action.

Structure lines

--line for ordinary hairlines, --line-strong where a table header or a swatch edge needs to hold, and --gold-hair where the hairline is doing brand work rather than layout work.

Contrast and accessibility

Body copy on paper uses --ink-soft, which clears WCAG AA comfortably at body sizes. Two combinations need care and are called out because they have caused real bugs:

CombinationRule
Faint ink on darkNever. --ink-faint is a light-ground token; on the dark band use --sage-soft. A featured package card once shipped with an illegible price label from exactly this mistake.
Clay on forestInsufficient contrast. On dark grounds an action button inverts to a paper or cream fill instead.
Gold as body textNever. Gold is for hairlines, small caps and emphasis at weight 600 — not for paragraphs.

Print note. These are screen values. The printed work was produced from the same hex values with the printer converting to CMYK; the dark band on the flyer is specified as #4A3020 rather than --forest, because the gradient does not survive a flat print well. See chapter 10.

Typography

Two faces, used with discipline.

Fraunces carries every display and heading; Hanken Grotesk carries everything else. Both are self-hosted as woff2 and ship inside the stylesheet — nothing is fetched from a font host at runtime.

Hanken Grotesk · body · weight 300–400 · line-height 1.72

Fundierte Wissenschaft · Persönliche Begleitung

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook05 · Typography

The typographic rules that matter most

1

Never hyphenate

Set hyphens: none and leave it. German compounds — Gesundheitscoaching, Frauengesundheit — are handled by reducing the type size until the word fits, never by breaking it.

2

The founder's name never breaks

“Desiree Gruber” stays on one line at every breakpoint. Wrap it in a non-breaking span wherever it appears near a fold.

3

Fluid sizes, not breakpoint jumps

Display type uses clamp() so it scales continuously. Check every headline at 360 px — that is where German breaks first.

4

Italic is an accent, not a voice

Fraunces italic marks the second clause of a headline or a single pulled phrase. A whole italic paragraph reads as a mistake.

5

Measure over size

Body copy caps at roughly 60 characters. Widening the column is never the fix for too much text — cutting the text is.

Multilingual setting

Every customer-facing surface exists in German, English and Spanish. German is the master language and is always the longest — which makes it the layout constraint. Two consequences for design:

  • Design in German first. A layout that holds in German holds in the other two. The reverse is not true, and English-first layouts routinely break when the German copy lands.
  • Headline sizes are per-language where needed. The printed flyer sets its A6 headline at 20.5 pt in English and Spanish but 17 pt in German. That is the rule 1 escape hatch in practice.

Where the faces come from. Both families are open-source and self-hosted in design-system/assets/fonts/ as latin and latin-ext woff2 subsets. Hanken Grotesk is a single variable file per subset covering weights 300–700 — if you ever re-download it, dedupe the @font-face rules or the bundle carries the same file five times.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook06 · Layout
06

Layout

Rhythm, width and tone.

The system has very little layout machinery on purpose: one container width, one vertical rhythm, and an alternation of grounds that paces a long page.

The container

--maxw is 1180px, with a fluid gutter --gut of clamp(20px,5vw,64px). Everything centres inside it. Full-bleed surfaces — image bands, dark sections — break the container but their content does not.

Vertical rhythm

Sections carry one of two paddings: the standard sec-pad or the tighter sec-pad-sm where two related sections should read as one movement. Do not invent intermediate values.

Tone alternation

Grounds cycle paper → cream → paper to pace the scroll, with a dark band placed deliberately — three or four times on a long page at most. The dark band is the page's punctuation; used more often it stops landing.

Grid

Two-column splits are asymmetric (roughly 0.95 / 1.05) rather than an even half — it reads as composed rather than divided. Package cards are a fixed three columns and collapse to one below 1024 px.

The whitespace budget

The single most common way to break this brand is to fill the space. The printed card is the calibration: roughly 4 % ink coverage. On screen that means few elements per viewport, one idea per section, and a willingness to let a headline sit alone above a large quiet area. If a design feels sparse next to a competitor's, it is probably correct.

Utility classes that exist and are safe to reuse: wrap (the max-width container), sec-pad / sec-pad-sm (vertical rhythm), u-kick (the kicker rule), em (the italic accent). Never invent a class name — nothing outside the shipped stylesheet resolves.

07

The component library

Twenty-two parts.

The real, shipped library — @auralis/design-system. Every component below is compiled code with a typed props contract and a written usage doc. This roster is generated from those docs, so it cannot drift from the code.

Foundations 4

ButtonThe one interactive element that carries an action. Everything else on an Auralis page is type, rule and photograph — so a button is loud by default, and its restraint is what makes it read as premium.
EmblemThe botanical seal — the recurring brand mark, and the only illustrative element in the system. It ships inside the stylesheet as a data URI, so it needs no image path and works offline.
LabelThe small uppercase, wide-tracked line that opens a section or annotates a value. It is the design system's orientation device: it tells the reader what kind of thing is coming before they read a word of the heading.
SparkThree dots — clay, then a slightly larger amber one, then clay again. The quietest signature in the brand, inherited from the printed documents where it separates movements of an argument.

Typography 5

DisplayThe largest editorial voice — Fraunces at a fluid clamp, set once per page for the hero headline. A second `Display` on a page destroys the hierarchy the first one creates.
EmThe brand's second voice: Fraunces italic, cinnamon-rust on light surfaces and amber gold on the dark bands.
HeadingSection and card headings, in Fraunces.
SignatureThe founder's hand-signed sign-off that closes the About section. It converts a page of claims into a person taking responsibility for them, which is the point of the whole section.
TextBody copy, in Hanken Grotesk.

Layout 2

SectionA full-width page section carrying the site's vertical rhythm and max-width wrap. Every block of the page is a `Section`; the page is a stack of them.
SectionHeadThe standard opening of a section: kicker label, title, optional lead paragraph. Using it instead of hand-assembling `Label` + `Heading` + `Text` is what keeps every section on the page starting on the same beat.
Modern Materia Medica11
Auralis Natura · Design Handbook07 · Components

Media 2

ImageBandA full-bleed photographic band with an optional caption plate. Its job is to let the page breathe between two dense sections — it is white space that happens to be a photograph.
PhotoFrameA photograph in the house frame: square corners, a soft wide shadow, and a gold hairline inset just inside the edge. It is how a person appears on an Auralis page.

Content 6

CredentialChipOne credential in the ribbon beneath the hero. Each chip leads with a glyph and states a single verifiable fact.
CredentialRibbonThe row of credential chips that sits immediately under the hero. Trust is established here, in the first screen, before any argument is made.
FaqItemOne question in the FAQ accordion. It manages its own open state.
FaqListThe accordion wrapper. It supplies the hairline rules between items and the column width that keeps answers readable.
MetaListThe credentials table: term on the left, value right-aligned, hairline between rows. Quiet and factual — and, on this site, the single most persuasive element on the page, because it is the only one that makes no argument at all.
TestimonialA client review on the dark testimonial band: stars, the quote, then an initial avatar with name and programme.

Commerce 3

CtaCardThe closing dark card that ends the page — the final ask, with the seal watermarked behind it.
PackageCardA pricing card — the commercial heart of the page.
PackageGridThe row that holds `PackageCard`s — three across on desktop, stacking on mobile with equal-height alignment.

Working with the library

Import the stylesheet once at the app root — every component styles itself through plain CSS classes, so without it everything renders unstyled:

import '@auralis/design-system/styles.css';
import { Section, Display, Em, Button } from '@auralis/design-system';

No provider and no context are needed. For your own layout glue, reach for the tokens via var(--*) rather than raw hex values.

If you needUse
A primary actionButton variant="clay" — exactly one per view.
A dark bandSection tone="dark" — three or four per page at most.
The pricing rowPackageGrid with exactly three PackageCards; featured inverts the middle one to the dark band.
A quiet brand momentEmblem in its watermark treatment.
Small caps above a headingLabel, or SectionHead when it also carries the heading. Both take onDark.

The stylesheet is shared with the live site. src/styles/components.css is the production homepage stylesheet, kept byte-identical apart from the token block. A fix made in one must be mirrored into the other in the same change, or the design system starts rendering against a stale sheet.

08

Composition

How a page is built.

The homepage is the reference composition. Its order is not arbitrary — it moves a stranger from recognition, through credibility, to a single free action.

#MovementBuilt from
1Hero — the promise, in the reader's own wordsSection · Display · Em · Button · seal watermark
2Credential ribbon — earn the right to be believed, immediately CredentialRibbon · CredentialChip
3The problem — name what she is feelingSection tone="dark" · Heading · Text
4The method — four movements, plainly explainedSection · SectionHead · MetaList
5An image band — let the page breatheImageBand
6Services and pricing — three programmes, one featured PackageGrid · PackageCard
7The founder — a face, a voice, a signaturePhotoFrame · Signature · Emblem
8Testimonials — real ones onlyTestimonial
9FAQ — answer the objections before they hardenFaqList · FaqItem
10The close — one free, no-obligation callCtaCard

Pacing rules

  • Alternate paper and cream between sections.
  • Never place two dark surfaces back to back.
  • One idea per section. If a section needs a sub-heading to hold together, it is two sections.
  • The primary CTA repeats — hero, mid-page, close — but only one is clay per viewport.

Adapting the pattern

A landing page for a single programme collapses movements 4–6 into one and keeps everything else. A corporate page swaps the pricing grid for a bespoke enquiry band. What never changes is the arc: promise → credibility → problem → method → proof → one action.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook09 · Writing the copy
09

Copy

German first, always.

Copy on this brand is not translated. It is written in German by the founder and then re-derived into English and Spanish — a change that lands in only one language is an unfinished change.

The workflow

German is the master. English and Spanish are re-derived from it in the same change, capturing the meaning and the register rather than the sentence structure. A literal translation of German marketing copy reads stiff in both.

Register

German uses the informal du throughout — this is a personal practice, not an institution. Keep sentences short enough to read aloud.

Words to use

Coaching. Begleitung. Bildung. Gesundheitscoaching. May support rather than will fix.

Words that are legally unavailable

Never “Ernährungsberaterin”, “Nutritionist” or “dietista-nutricionista” — a protected profession in Spain under Ley 44/2003. Never “heilt”, “cures”, “diagnose”, “treats” or “garantiert”.

Naming

The three programmes are localised, and the internal keys never change:

KeyGermanEnglishSpanishPrice
rootKlarheitClarityClaridad€199
bloomWandelChangeCambio€399 · 4 weeks
flourishBalanceBalanceEquilibrio€899 · 12 weeks
corpVerbindungConnectionConexiónTailored

Never state a duration for the free call. It is a Kennenlerngespräch / introductory call / llamada de presentación — free and no-obligation, with no minutes named anywhere on a customer-facing surface. This is a standing founder decision.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook10 · Print production
10

Print

Ink on paper.

Two finished pieces define the printed brand: the business card (design 5B “Reine Fläche”) and the A5/A6 flyer in three languages. Their geometry is load-bearing and must not be “corrected”.

Flyer formats

FormatTrimBleed boxPage boxLanguages
A6 (narrowed)95 × 148 mm101 × 154 mm111 × 164 mmEN · DE · ES
A5 (narrowed)138 × 210 mm144 × 216 mm154 × 226 mmEN · DE · ES

Both formats are 10 mm narrower than the DIN standard at unchanged height. This is deliberate — it moves the proportion nearer the golden ratio. It is not an error, and a printer or designer who “fixes” it back to DIN has broken the piece.

Page construction

  • Page box — the sheet the browser prints: trim, plus 3 mm bleed on every side, plus 5 mm of margin for the crop marks.
  • Artboard — an absolutely positioned div at left:5mm; top:5mm, sized to the bleed box. All artwork lives here; overflow:hidden clips the bleed.
  • Crop marks — eight 0.15 mm hairlines in #aaa39a, drawn 1 mm outside the trim edge and 4 mm long, plus a caption strip naming language, side, trim and bleed.

The registration rule — learned the hard way. No page's geometry may depend on its content. An early version let the artboard flow, and the back side printed roughly 20 mm higher on the sheet than the front. Every page is now a fixed page box with the artboard at a fixed offset, and the repository's CI print check (ci/check-print.mjs) asserts it. Keep that check in any new print piece.

Modern Materia Medica16
Auralis Natura · Design Handbook10 · Print production

Specifying a new piece

Units

Everything is specified in millimetres and points, never CSS pixels. Reproduce values exactly — a measure that looks “roughly 6 mm” is 6 mm.

Vertical rhythm

Built from explicit height:*mm; flex:none spacer divs rather than margins, so the stack cannot collapse or drift between browsers.

The dark band

Print uses a flat #4A3020, not the screen gradient — 46 mm tall on A6, 58 mm on A5, anchored with margin-top:auto.

Front-face proportions (A6 → A5)

ElementA6A5
Top spacer10 mm19 mm
Seal16 × 16 mm24 × 24 mm
Gold rule14 × 0.25 mm20 × 0.25 mm
Headline20.5 pt
(DE 17 pt)		29 pt
(DE 24 pt)
Lede8.6 pt / 80 mm11 pt / 112 mm

Sending to a printer

  • Export at 300 dpi with bleed included and crop marks on.
  • Let the printer handle CMYK conversion from the supplied hex values — the palette was proofed this way.
  • Choose an uncoated or lightly textured stock. The design is built around low ink coverage, and a gloss finish fights it.
  • Ask for a physical proof before any run above a few hundred pieces. The gold hairlines are the first thing to disappear on a cheap press.

The 4 % rule

The approved business card prints at roughly 4 % ink coverage. When a new printed piece is designed, measure it against that number. If it is dramatically heavier, the design has stopped trusting the paper — and on this brand, the paper is doing the premium work.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook11 · Photography
11

Photography

Real light, real hands.

The photography is documentary rather than styled: natural light, real workspaces, and the founder actually working. It is the warmth half of the brand's promise.

Portrait. Desk, daylight, direct gaze. The hero and About treatment.

In practice. A consultation in progress — credibility without a claim.

Still life. Food and botanicals, uncomposed. Used for image bands.

Direction

  • Natural, soft, directional light — never flash, never a studio sweep.
  • Warm neutrals that sit with the palette: wood, linen, ceramic, green leaf.
  • Real spaces with real texture. Nothing looks propped.
  • People are working or listening, not smiling at the lens holding a salad.

Treatment

Images are placed inside PhotoFrame or run full-bleed as an ImageBand. A hairline border, never a rounded corner, never a drop shadow. Cropping is done with object-fit: cover and an explicit objectPosition — never by distorting the frame.

Never

  • Never substitute stock imagery on this brand. If a real photograph does not exist, ship a placeholder and flag it — the documentary quality is the point, and generic wellness stock destroys it immediately.
  • No heavy filters, no duotones, no colour grading away from the natural warmth.
  • No text baked into a photograph. Type sits in the layout, over a quiet area if it must overlap.

One image carries context. desiree-womens-health.jpg shows the founder visibly pregnant and sits in the Frauengesundheit section by explicit founder decision. Do not move it into an About or motherhood context, and check with the founder before writing any copy near it.

Auralis Natura · Design Handbook12 · Guardrails
12

Content guardrails

Rules that are law, not taste.

These constrain every word and image produced for this business. They are not style preferences and they are never relaxed to make something punchier.

1

Coaching and education — never medical care

In Spain, dietista-nutricionista is a legally protected profession under Ley 44/2003. Position everything as holistic health coaching and education: lifestyle, habits, general nutrition education, accountability. Never diagnosis, treatment of disease, or prescriptive medical nutrition therapy.

2

“Dr.” means Dr. rer. nat.

An academic doctorate in bioorganic chemistry, disclosed plainly wherever the title appears. Never imply a physician. That honesty is itself a brand asset.

3

Complement, never replace, medical care

Refer out. Keep red-flag guidance and the emergency note — “see your doctor, call 112 in an emergency” — in every client-facing deliverable.

4

Testimonials are real, or they do not exist

Never invent, embellish or composite a review — in production, in a mockup, or in a component preview. Placeholders must be visibly labelled as such.

5

Health data is GDPR special category

Explicit consent, a lawful basis, data minimisation, EU-hosted encrypted storage, a defined retention period. Never route health details through social media, DMs or messaging apps.

6

AI is assistive and human-led

Any AI-drafted client output is reviewed, edited and approved by the founder before it reaches a client. Educational, never diagnostic.

7

Figures are directional

Market and financial numbers are estimates framed for validation — never presented as forecasts or fundraising-grade figures.

Design implication. These are not only a copywriter's problem. A layout that has no room for a disclaimer, a testimonial component with no placeholder state, or a form that collects health data without a consent field are all design failures. Build the space for compliance into the composition from the start.

Asset inventory

What ships in this package.

Everything referenced in this handbook travels with it. Paths are relative to the root of the ZIP.

PathWhat it is
01-handbook/This document, as PDF and as self-contained HTML.
02-design-system/The built, browser-ready bundle of @auralis/design-system: 22 compiled components, typed props, per-component usage docs, tokens, fonts, and a preview card for every component.
03-brand-masters/The best copies of the seal that exist — full colour at 1600 px, gold on dark, single-colour brown, the watermark variant, and the website QR code.
04-print/The approved business card (design 5B) and the A5/A6 trilingual flyer as production artwork, plus their handoff notes and the CI print check.
05-fonts/Fraunces and Hanken Grotesk as self-hosted woff2, latin and latin-ext, with the @font-face CSS.
06-photography/The real photography library — portraits, consultation, still life, certificates.
07-website/The live homepage as a single HTML file — the canonical, shipped expression of everything in this handbook.

Using the design system

02-design-system/ is the format Claude Design consumes directly: _ds_bundle.js exposes every component on window.AuralisNatura, styles.css carries the whole style closure including the self-hosted fonts, and each component ships a .d.ts contract, a .prompt.md usage reference and an .html preview card. Upload its contents at the project root.

One last thing
